h: Loving Hashem with Body Soul and Wealth

p: "וַיָּבֹא יַעֲקֹב שָׁלֵם" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לג, יח) – דָּרְשׁוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת לג עַמּוּד ב):
— And Jacob came whole (Genesis 33:18)—they expounded in the Gemara (Shabbat 33b):
"שָׁלֵם בְּגוּפוֹ, שָׁלֵם בְּמָמוֹנוֹ, שָׁלֵם בְּתוֹרָתוֹ".
— "whole in his body, whole in his wealth, whole in his Torah."
וְהַשְּׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים הֵם כְּנֶגֶד מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ, וּבְכָל נַפְשְׁךָ, וּבְכָל מְאֹדֶךָ" (דְּבָרִים ו, ה):
— And these three expressions of wholeness correspond to the three requirements of loving God: "with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might":

p: "שָׁלֵם בְּגוּפוֹ" – שֶׁנִּתְרַפֵּא מִצַּלְעָתוֹ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (עט, ה);
— "Whole in his body"—he was healed from his limping, as written in Bereishit Rabbah (79:5);
וְהַיְינוּ דְּמִקּוֹדֶם כְּתִיב: "וַיַּרְא כִּי לֹא יָכֹל לוֹ וַיִּגַּע בְּכַף יְרֵכוֹ" (שָׁם לב, כו),
— for previously it was written: "And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh",
שֶׁאַחַר שֶׁרָאָה הַסַּמָּאֵ"ל שֶׁעַל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּעַצְמוֹ אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם מְקוֹם קִטְרוּג,
— whereby once Samael saw that against Jacob's personal essence he had no basis for prosecution,
"וַיִּגַּע בְּכַף יְרֵכוֹ" – בְּזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁעֲתִידִין לַעֲמוֹד מִמֶּנּוּ, דְּשָׁם מָצָא עוֹד מָקוֹם לְקַטְרֵג;
— he struck the hollow of his thigh—striking the future descendants destined to issue from his loins, where he found room to accuse;
וְאַחַר שֶׁנִּצְּחוֹ, נִתְרַפֵּא מִצַּלְעָתוֹ, שֶׁהוּא שֶׁמִּטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה, דִּכְתִיב: "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים" (יְשַׁעְיָה ס, כא);
— and once Jacob prevailed over him, he was healed from his limp, proving that his bed was whole and "Your people are all righteous";
וְזֶהוּ נֶגֶד "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ" שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק הָרוֹאֶה, בְּרָכוֹת נד עַמּוּד א): "בִּשְׁנֵי יְצָרֶיךָ – בְּיֵצֶר טוֹב וּבְיֵצֶר רָע",
— and this corresponds to "with all your heart," expounded in Berakhot (54a) as: "with both your inclinations—with the good inclination and the evil inclination",
וְזֶהוּ "שָׁלֵם בְּגוּפוֹ", שֶׁכָּל גּוּפוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן בִּקְדוּשָּׁה.
— which is "whole in his body," all physical bodies of Israel sharing this bodily holiness.

Intact in his wealth; although, Rabbi Avun said in the name of Rav Aḥa: Our patriarch Jacob would give Esau that same gift for nine years; nevertheless, here, intact in his wealth. paragraphs.text: Berakhot 54a: “The mishna articulates a general principle: One is obligated to recite a blessing for the bad that befalls him just as he recites a blessing for the good that befalls him, as it is stated: ‘And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might’ (Deuteronomy 6:5). The mishna explains this verse as follows: ‘With all your heart’ means with your two inclinations, with your good inclination and your evil inclination, both of which must be subjugated to the love of God. ‘With all your soul’ means even if God takes your soul. ‘And with all your might’ means with all your money, as money is referred to in the Bible as might. Alternatively, it may be explained that ‘with all your might’ means with every measure that He metes out to you; whether it is good or troublesome, thank Him.”

p: "שָׁלֵם בְּתוֹרָתוֹ" – הוּא "בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ",
— "Whole in his Torah"—corresponds to "with all your soul",
דִּכְתִיב: "נֵר ה' נִשְׁמַת אָדָם" (מִשְׁלֵי כ, כז), וּכְתִיב: "נֵר לְרַגְלִי דְבָרֶךָ וְאוֹר לִנְתִיבָתִי" (תְּהִלִּים קיט, קה), שֶׁהוּא תּוֹרָה אוֹר.
— for it is written: "The candle of Hashem is the soul of man" (Proverbs 20:27), and: "Your word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path" (Psalms 119:105), Torah being light.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁכָּל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם כְּלַל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
— Meaning that all the souls of Israel embody the totality of the teachings of the Torah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסִפְרֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ: יִשְׂרָאֵ"ל רָאשֵׁי תֵּיבוֹת: יֵ'שׁ שִׁ'שִּׁים רִ'בּוֹא אוֹ'תִיּוֹת לַ'תּוֹרָה;
— as written in sacred books: the name Yisrael (ישראל) is an acronym for: "There are sixty myriads of letters in the Torah";
וְהַיְינוּ דְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל הוּא אוֹת אוֹ חֵלֶק מֵאוֹת מֵאוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה,
— every soul of Israel corresponding to a letter or part of a letter of the Torah,
וְהוּא הַמֵּאִיר וּמוֹרֶה דֶּרֶךְ לְהַנֶּפֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
— which illuminates and guides the path for that Jewish soul.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים ח עַמּוּד א): "לָמָּה צַדִּיקִים דּוֹמִין בִּפְנֵי שְׁכִינָה? כְּנֵר בִּפְנֵי הָאֲבוּקָה",
— And this is what they asked (Pesachim 8a): "To what are the righteous compared before the Shechinah? To a candle before a blazing torch",
וְזֶהוּ "שָׁלֵם בְּתוֹרָתוֹ", שֶׁכָּל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּקְדוּשָּׁה.
— and this is "whole in his Torah," all souls of Israel being rooted in holiness.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 8a: “The Gemara asks: And is the light of a torch not bright enough for searching? But didn’t Rava say: What is the meaning of that which is written, ‘And a brightness appears as the light; He has rays at His side; and there is the hiding of His power’ (Habakkuk 3:4), which indicates that God will provide rays of glory for the righteous in the future? The Sages explained this verse by means of a parable: To what are the righteous comparable before the Divine Presence? They are comparable to a lamp in the face of a torch. This statement indicates that the light of a torch is significantly greater than that of a lamp, and consequently a torch should be more effective in the search for leaven. And likewise Rava said: One who uses a torch for the blessing over fire in havdala has performed the mitzva in the optimal manner. Apparently, the light of a torch is greater than that of a lamp.”

p: "שָׁלֵם בְּמָמוֹנוֹ" – נֶגֶד "וּבְכָל מְאֹדֶךָ",
— "Whole in his wealth"—corresponds to "with all your might (me'odekha)",
שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת סא עַמּוּד ב): "וְאִם יֵשׁ לְךָ אָדָם שֶׁמָּמוֹנוֹ חָבִיב עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ כו'".
— which the Gemara (Berakhot 61b) expounds: "if there is a person whose wealth is more precious to him than his body, therefore it says with all your might (wealth)".
וְלִכְאוֹרָה: אֵיךְ יִתָּכֵן שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מִי שֶׁמָּמוֹנוֹ חָבִיב עָלָיו יוֹתֵר מִגּוּפוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לוֹ "וְאָהַבְתָּ וְגוֹמֵר"?
— Now seemingly: how can it be that anyone would cherish money more than his physical life, requiring a special verse to command him?
אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת יֵשׁ לָשׁוֹן זֶה בַּגְּמָרָא (חֻלִּין צא עַמּוּד א)
— However, in truth this exact phrasing is used in Chullin (91a)
גַּבֵּי צַדִּיקִים: "שֶׁמָּמוֹנָם חָבִיב עֲלֵיהֶם יוֹתֵר מִגּוּפָם, לְפִי שֶׁאֵין פּוֹשְׁטִין יְדֵיהֶם בְּגֶזֶל";
— regarding the righteous: "their wealth is more precious to them than their bodies, because they never stretch forth their hands in robbery";
וְכֵן מָצִינוּ (תַּעֲנִית כג עַמּוּד ב) בְּאַבָּא חִלְקִיָּה שֶׁאָמַר: "זֶה מַעֲלֶה אֲרוּכָה וְזֶה אֵינָהּ מַעֲלָה אֲרוּכָה" (שֶׁחָס עַל כְּסוּתוֹ יוֹתֵר מִבְּשָׂרוֹ).
— and so in Ta'anit (23b) regarding Abba Chilkiyah, who spared his garments over his flesh because torn flesh heals on its own whereas torn clothing does not.
וְהַטַּעַם: שֶׁכֵּיוָן שֶׁרְכוּשָׁם הוּא רַק מַה שֶּׁנּוֹתֵן לָהֶם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
— And the reason is: since the wealth of tzaddikim consists purely of what Hashem bestows upon them directly,
וְיוֹדְעִים שֶׁהָרְכוּשׁ שַׁיָּיךְ לָהֶם לְעִיקַּר שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחַיִּים, עַל כֵּן חָבִיב עֲלֵיהֶם (וְנִתְבָּאֵר מַאֲמָר ו).
— and they know that every asset is allocated to them for their essential mission of life, it is cherished as a sacred trust (explained in Discourse 6).

p: וְכֵן יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נִצְטַעֵר עַל הַדּוֹרוֹן שֶׁשָּׁלַח לְעֵשָׂו,
— And so our father Jacob was deeply pained over the tribute gift sent to Esau,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה עו, ח): "'וַתַּעֲבֹר הַמִּנְחָה עַל פָּנָיו' (בְּרֵאשִׁית לב, כב) – אַף הוּא בְּעָקָא",
— as written in Bereishit Rabbah (76:8): "'So the present passed over before him'—he too was in distress",
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁכְּבָר הָיָה לוֹ הָעֲדָרִים מְבוֹרָרִין אֶצְלוֹ,
— meaning that his flocks had already been completely clarified in holiness,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא עֲדָרִים
— having 600,000 flocks
– וְהַיְינוּ כְּמִסְפַּר שׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁמִּכָּל אֶחָד יִהְיֶה עֵדֶר שָׁלֵם –
— corresponding to the 600,000 root souls of Israel, each one becoming a complete flock—
וְכָאן רָאָה שֶׁהֻוצְרַךְ לִשְׁלוֹחַ מֵהֶם לְעֵשָׂו, וְהָיָה לוֹ צַעַר מִזֶּה שֶׁמָּא אֵין רְכוּשׁוֹ מְבוֹרָר עוֹד.
— and when compelled to send hundreds of them to Esau, he grieved lest his possessions were not yet fully purified.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְבָּרֵר לוֹ שֶׁהוּא "שָׁלֵם בְּמָמוֹנוֹ",
— And subsequently it was made clear that he was "whole in his wealth",
וְלֹא חָסַר כְּלוּם מֵאוֹתוֹ דּוֹרוֹן,
— having lost nothing through that tribute gift;
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה שַׁיָּיךְ לְעֵשָׂו שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת בָּהֶם, וְעַל יְדֵי הַדּוֹרוֹן הוֹצִיא מִמֶּנּוּ הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ.
— for those specific animals belonged to Esau's domain, and through that gift Jacob extracted the holy sparks trapped within Esau, as explained.

h: The Evil Inclination Disguised as a Scholar

p: אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת הַכֹּל אֶחָד:
— However, in truth all three explanations are one:
שֶׁבְּעִנְיַן הַשַּׂר שֶׁנִּזְדַּוֵּוג לוֹ בַּדֶּרֶךְ אִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (חֻלִּין צא עַמּוּד א): כְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם נִדְמָה לוֹ.
— for regarding the angel who confronted him, the Gemara states: he appeared as a Torah scholar.
וְהוּא שֶׁזֶּה כֹּחַ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, שֶׁלִּפְעָמִים מִתְחַפֵּשׂ כְּמוֹרֶה דֶּרֶךְ לְטוֹבָה,
— And this is the cunning power of the yetzer hara, which disguises itself as a teacher of righteousness,
וְאוֹמֵר לְרַע שֶׁהוּא טוֹב, וְשָׂם חֹשֶׁךְ לְאוֹר;
— calling evil good, and putting darkness for light;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּכָל הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה מְלָכִים וְאַרְבָּעָה הֶדְיוֹטוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ גְּדוֹלִים בַּתּוֹרָה:
— as we find regarding the three kings and four commoners enumerated in the Mishnah who were towering masters of Torah:

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיָרָבְעָם (סַנְהֶדְרִין קב עַמּוּד א): "בְּשַׂלְמָה חֲדָשָׁה – שֶׁחִדְּשׁוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁלֹּא שָׁמְעָה אֹזֶן מֵעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁכָּל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים דּוֹמִין לִפְנֵיהֶם כְּעִשְׂבֵּי הַשָּׂדֶה";
— as written of Jeroboam: "clad in a new garment—they innovated insights that no ear had ever heard, all other sages appearing before them like grass of the field";
וְכֵן בְּדוֹאֵג וַאֲחִיתֹפֶל אִיתָא (שָׁם קו עַמּוּד ב): אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת בַּעְיָא בָּעוּ דּוֹאֵג וַאֲחִיתֹפֶל וְכוּלֵי;
— and of Doeg and Ahithophel: they raised 400 deep halakhic dilemmas on a single topic;
וְגַם עַל גֵּיחֲזִי אִיתָא (בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי סַנְהֶדְרִין פֶּרֶק י הֲלָכָה ב): גֵּיחֲזִי אָדָם גִּבּוֹר בַּתּוֹרָה הָיָה וְכוּלֵי;
— and of Gehazi in the Yerushalmi: Gehazi was a mighty giant in Torah;
וְאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (שָׁם קג עַמּוּד ב): מְנַשֶּׁה הָיָה שׁוֹנֶה נ"ה (חֲמִשִּׁים וְחָמֵשׁ) פָּנִים בְּתוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים, אַחְאָב פ"ה (שְׁמוֹנִים וְחָמֵשׁ), יָרָבְעָם ק"ג (מֵאָה וְשָׁלֹשׁ) –
— and the Gemara relates: Menashe expounded 55 facets of Torat Kohanim, Ahab 85, and Jeroboam 103—
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמִנְיַן "עֵגֶ"ל" (103) הָיָה דּוֹרֵשׁ פָּנִים בְּתוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים,
— expounding 103 interpretations equaling the numerical value of egel (calf = 103),
שֶׁהָיָה אוֹמֵר שֶׁהוּא עִנְיַן עֲבוֹדָה לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
— arguing with brilliant proofs that the golden calves were authentic divine service,
דְּאִם לֹא כֵן לֹא הָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַבְּלִים מִמֶּנּוּ;
— for otherwise Israel would never have accepted them from him;

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (שָׁם קא סוֹף עַמּוּד ב): "סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דְּגַבְרָא כְּיָרָבְעָם פָּלַח לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְכוּלֵי? יֵהוּא צַדִּיקָא רַבָּא הֲוָה וְכוּלֵי, חוֹתָמוֹ שֶׁל אֲחִיָּה הַשִּׁילוֹנִי רָאָה וְטָעָה", עַיֵּין שָׁם.

— as stated in Sanhedrin (101b): "Could it enter your mind that a man of Jeroboam's stature would worship simple idols? Jehu was a great tzaddik, but he saw the signature of Ahijah the Shilonite on the document and was misled," see there.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהֵם סָבְרוּ שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת הוּא עִנְיַן עֲבוֹדָה לַשָּׁמַיִם,
— Meaning that they self-deceptively rationalized that their path was service of Heaven,
וְלָהֶם נַעֲשׂוּ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁלָּמְדוּ סַמָּא דְּמוֹתָא לַמַּשְׂמְאִילִים בָּהּ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שַׁבָּת פח עַמּוּד ב).
— and for them the Torah they studied became a potion of death because they turned to the left.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 88b: “And that is what Rava said: To those who are right-handed in their approach to Torah, and engage in its study with strength, good will, and sanctity, Torah is a drug of life, and to those who are left-handed in their approach to Torah, it is a drug of death. Alternatively, why are matters of Torah referred to as royal? Because to each and every utterance that emerged from the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He, two crowns are tied. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: What is the meaning of that which is written: ‘My beloved is to me like a bundle of myrrh that lies between my breasts’ (Song of Songs 1:13)? The Congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, even though my beloved, God, causes me suffering and bitterness, He still lies between my breasts. And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi interpreted the verse: ‘My beloved is to me like a cluster (eshkol) of henna (hakofer) in the vineyards of (karmei) Ein Gedi’ (Song of Songs 1:14). He, Whom everything (shehakol) is His, forgives (mekhapper) me for the sin of the kid (gedi), i.e., the calf, that I collected (shekaramti) for myself. The Gemara explains: From where is it inferred that the word in this verse, karmei, is a term of gathering? Mar Zutra, son of Rav Naḥman, said that it is as we learned in a mishna: A launderer’s chair upon which one gathers (koremim) the garments.”

p: וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ "כְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם נִדְמָה לוֹ":
— And this is why the Gemara states: "he appeared to Jacob as a Torah scholar":
רַק שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב מִדָּתוֹ אֱמֶת,
— only that Jacob's attribute was absolute Truth,
וְלֹא יָכֹל לְהַטְעוֹתוֹ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם;
— so the angel could not mislead him in the slightest, Heaven forbid;
"וַיִּגַּע בְּכַף יְרֵכוֹ" – שֶׁבְּתוֹלְדוֹתָיו יוּכַל עוֹד לְקַטְרֵג וְלִכְנוֹס וּלְהַטְעוֹת;
— whereupon the angel struck the hollow of his thigh—seeking to infiltrate and deceive future generations;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁנִּתְרַפֵּא מִצַּלְעָתוֹ, הַיְינוּ שֶׁרָאָה יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לִשְׁלוֹט בְּזַרְעוֹ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְהַטְעוֹתָם, שֶׁיִּתְבָּרְרוּ אַחַר כָּךְ.
— and when Jacob was healed from his limping, it demonstrated that the yetzer hara would never permanently corrupt his seed, all of whom would ultimately be refined.
וְזֶהוּ "שָׁלֵם בְּתוֹרָתוֹ" – שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע לְקַלְקֵל עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה, שֶׁיִּתְעֶה לִהְיוֹת לַמַּשְׂמְאִילִים בָּהּ,
— And this is "whole in his Torah"—that the yetzer hara could not distort Torah to turn them to the left,
וְזֶהוּ כְּנֶגֶד "בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ" כָּאָמוּר.
— corresponding to "with all your soul," as stated.

h: Jacob Discovers the Source of His Help

p: וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה (רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּצֵא סח, ב)
— And this clarifies what is written in Bereishit Rabbah (68:2)
שֶׁבַּהֲלִיכָתוֹ לְבֵית לָבָן אָמַר:
— that when Jacob journeyed to Laban's house, he exclaimed:
"'אֶשָּׂא עֵינַי אֶל הֶהָרִים' (תְּהִלִּים קכא, א) – אֶל הַהוֹרִים: לִמְלַפְּנַי וּלְמַעֲבְדַנַי, 'מֵאַיִן יָבֹא עֶזְרִי'".
— "'I will lift up my eyes unto the hills (he-harim)'—unto my parents and teachers (horim): unto those who taught me and those who brought me into being; 'from whence shall my help come?'"
וְהַיְינוּ כֵּיוָן שֶׁרָאָה שֶׁהֻוצְרַךְ לִבְרוֹחַ מִפְּנֵי עֵשָׂו וְלֵילֵךְ לְבֵית לָבָן,
— For when he saw that he was forced to flee from Esau to the house of Laban,
סָבוּר שֶׁלֹּא הוֹעִיל לוֹ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁלִּמְּדוּהוּ רַבּוֹתָיו שֶׁהֵבִיאוּ בוֹ הַנְּשָׁמָה – "נֵר ה' נִשְׁמַת אָדָם", וְזֶהוּ "לִמְלַפְּנַי";
— he feared that the Torah taught to him by his masters (Shem and Eber) who elevated his soul had not shielded him, this being 'those who taught me';
וְגַם קְדוּשַׁת הַגּוּף שֶׁזָּכָה עַל יְדֵי אֲבוֹתָיו יִצְחָק וְרִבְקָה, שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמַר "וּלְמַעֲבְדַנַי" שֶׁהֵם הֱבִיאוּהוּ לָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה:
— and likewise regarding the holiness of his body inherited from Isaac and Rebecca, 'those who brought me into being':
וְיִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נוֹלַד בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
— for Isaac was born in pristine holiness,
וְגַם רִבְקָה כְּשֶׁהָיְתָה בַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים כְּבָר זָכְתָה לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ גְּמִילוּת חֲסָדִים שֶׁאָמְרָה: "גַּם לִגְמַלֶּיךָ אֶשְׁאָב" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כד, יט),
— and Rebecca already at age three embodied lovingkindness, drawing water for the camels;
וְצָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת גּוּפוֹ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה עַל יְדֵי שֶׁבָּא מִיִּצְחָק וְרִבְקָה,
— such that Jacob's body was invested with supreme purity;
וְעַתָּה הוּא מוּכְרָח לֵילֵךְ לְבֵית לָבָן – "מֵאַיִן יָבֹא עֶזְרִי?".
— yet now he was compelled to enter the corrupt house of Laban, crying: 'From whence shall my help come?'

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 68:2: “Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥman began: ‘A song of ascents. I lift my eyes to the mountains (heharim)’ (Psalms 121:1) – I lift my eyes to the parents (hahorim), to my teachers, and to those who raised me. ‘From where will my help come?’ (Psalms 121:1) – Eliezer, when he went to bring Rebecca, what is written in his regard: ‘The slave took ten camels…’ (Genesis 24:10), but I (Jacob) do not have even one nose ring or one bracelet. Rabbi Ḥanina said: He (Isaac) sent him empty-handed. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: He sent with him, but Esau arose and took it from him. He then said: ‘What, will I lose my confidence in my Creator? God forbid, I will not lose my confidence in my Creator.’ Instead, ‘My help is from the Lord’ (Psalms 121:2). ‘He will not let your foot give way; He who watches over you will not slumber’ (Psalms 121:3). ‘Behold, (the Guardian of Israel) neither slumbers nor sleeps…’ (Psalms 121:4). The Lord will guard you from all evil" (Psalms 121:7) – from Esau and from Laban; ‘He will guard your life’ (Psalms 121:7) – from the angel of death. ‘The Lord will guard your going and your coming’ (Psalms 121:8) – ‘Jacob departed.’”

— And then he realized: "My help comes from Hashem, Who made heaven and earth",
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עִיקַּר הָעוֹשֶׂה הַגּוּף וְהַנְּשָׁמָה,
— meaning that Hashem is the ultimate Fashioner of both soul and body,
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁדָּרְשׁוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין צא עַמּוּד ב): "'יִקְרָא אֶל הַשָּׁמַיִם מֵעָל' – זוֹ נְשָׁמָה, 'וְאֶל הָאָרֶץ' – זֶה הַגּוּף";
— as expounded in Sanhedrin (91b): "'He calls to the heavens from above'—this is the soul; 'and to the earth'—this is the body";
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה וַדַּאי עִיקָּרָהּ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהוּא הַמּוֹפִיעַ בָּאָדָם הַתּוֹרָה – "נֵר לְרַגְלִי דְבָרֶךָ", שֶׁהוּא "נֵר ה' וְגוֹמֵר";
— the soul deriving directly from Hashem Who illuminates it with Torah;
וְאַף הַגּוּף, שֶׁאֲבוֹתָיו הֵם שֻׁתָּפִים בּוֹ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָעִיקָּר הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
— and even the physical body, in which parents are partners (Niddah 31a), is primarily fashioned by Hashem.

h: Jacob and Moses Secure the Holiness of Israel

p: וְכָאן נִתְבָּרֵר לוֹ אַחַר שֶׁנִּצַּח לְשָׂרוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו:
— And here, after defeating the angel of Esau, it was fully revealed to him:
שֶׁהוּא "שָׁלֵם בְּגוּפוֹ" – וְכָל גּוּפֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּקְדוּשָּׁה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים";
— that he was "whole in his body"—all bodies of Israel sharing holy preservation;

"וְשָׁלֵם בְּתוֹרָתוֹ" – נֶגֶד הַנְּשָׁמָה, שֶׁלֹּא יוּכְלוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְקַלְקֵל בְּפִיתּוּי הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּתְעוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בְּהַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לִהְיוֹת לַמַּשְׂמְאִילִים בָּהּ.
— and "whole in his Torah"—facing the soul, ensuring that the yetzer hara cannot permanently mislead them into turning Torah into a deadly poison.
וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בְּתִקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן יג, כט עַמּוּד א):
— And this is what is stated in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 13, 29a):
"וְיַעֲקֹב וְכוּלֵי, אִתְּמַר בְּיַעֲקֹב: 'וַיָּבֹא יַעֲקֹב שָׁלֵם', וְיַעֲקֹב וַדַּאי אִיהוּ דִּיוֹקְנָא דְּעַמּוּדָא דְּאֶמְצָעִיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּלְבַר;
— "'And Jacob came whole'—Jacob is the outward manifestation of the Central Column;
וְהָא מֹשֶׁה תַּמָּן הֲוָה, אֶלָּא מִסִּטְרָא דִּלְגָאו הֲוָה, דָּא מִגּוּפָא וְדָא מִנִּשְׁמָתָא", עַיֵּין שָׁם.
— and Moses was there too, being its inward soul—this one (Jacob) is the body, and that one (Moses) is the soul," see there.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ יָצְאוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל, בֵּירֵר כָּל גּוּפֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם בִּקְדוּשָּׁה;
— For our father Jacob, from whom all Israel issued, purified the physical bodies of Israel into holiness;
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ שֶׁהוֹרִיד כָּל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא כְּלַל נִשְׁמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל, הוּא נִשְׁמָתָא – שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הַנְּשָׁמוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
— while Moses our teacher who brought down the Torah is the soul of all Jewish souls.
וְיַעֲקֹב זָכָה אָז לְזַרְעוֹ גַּם כֵּן שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ.
— And Jacob then secured for his descendants that they would merit the Giving of the Torah through Moses.

p: "וְשָׁלֵם בְּמָמוֹנוֹ" – הוּא בְּוַדַּאי מֵעִנְיַן עֵשָׂו,
— And "whole in his wealth"—is certainly connected to his encounter with Esau,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַדּוֹרוֹן שֶׁהָיָה שַׁיָּיךְ לְעֵשָׂו הוֹצִיא מִמֶּנּוּ כָּל הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת שֶׁהָיָה בוֹ, וְכָל הַחָכְמָה שֶׁהָיָה כָּלוּל בּוֹ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ.
— for through the gift belonging to Esau, Jacob extracted from him all the captive holy sparks and intellect, as stated.

h: Shabbat Restores Every Dimension of Wholeness

p: וּבְשַׁבָּת כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל שָׁלֵם בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה אֵלּוּ:
— And on Shabbat, every Jew merits all three dimensions of wholeness:
"שָׁלֵם בְּגוּפוֹ" – שֶׁכָּל הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
— "Whole in his body"—for on Shabbat all physical bodily pleasure is sanctified,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה: שֶׁאַף כְּשֶׁמְּכַוֵּון בְּשַׁבָּת לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ, הוּא גַּם כֵּן בִּקְדוּשָּׁה;
— as the holy Ari wrote: even when eating for personal gratification on Shabbat, the enjoyment is sanctified;
"וְשָׁלֵם בְּתוֹרָתוֹ" – דְּכוּלֵי עָלְמָא בְּשַׁבָּת נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת פו עַמּוּד ב),
— "and whole in his Torah"—for all agree that the Torah was given on Shabbat,
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, מז עַמּוּד ב): "בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי – דָּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה דְּאִיהוּ יוֹם שְׁבִיעִי", וְהַיְינוּ מַלְכוּת פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה;
— and in the Zohar: "'On the seventh day'—this is the Oral Torah," which is Malchut;
"וְשָׁלֵם בְּמָמוֹנוֹ" – דְּאִיתָא (שַׁבָּת קיט עַמּוּד א):
— "and whole in his wealth"—as taught in Shabbat (119a):
"וְשֶׁבִּשְׁאָר אֲרָצוֹת בִּשְׁבִיל מַה הֵם מִתְעַשְּׁרִים? בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁמְּכַבְּדִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי,
— "And those wealthy Jews in the Diaspora, in what merit do they prosper? In merit of honoring Shabbat,
וּכְשֶׁמַּנִּיחִים אוֹתָהּ (אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָן הֶעָמוּס) אוֹמְרִים: 'לַה' הָאָרֶץ וּמְלוֹאָהּ וְגוֹמֵר'", עַיֵּין שָׁם;
— and when they set down the laden table, they proclaim: 'The earth is Hashem's and the fullness thereof' (Psalms 24:1)", see there;
וְהַיְינוּ: אַף שֶׁזָּכָה לְעֹשֶׁר מוּפְלָג עַל יְדֵי שֶׁכִּבֵּד אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת, לֹא הֵזִיק לוֹ הָעֹשֶׁר,
— meaning that even while acquiring vast wealth through honoring Shabbat, riches never corrupted him,
וְהָיָה מַכִּיר כִּי לַה' הָאָרֶץ וְהוּא הַנּוֹתֵן.
— for he continuously recognized that the earth is Hashem's and He is the sole Giver.
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַשְּׁלֵימוּת בְּמָמוֹן: שֶׁכֵּיוָן שֶׁהוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵינוֹ מַזִּיק כְּלָל.
— And this is the essence of wholeness in wealth: when perceived as arriving directly from Hashem, it never harms the soul.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה יא, א): "'בִּרְכַּת ה' הִיא תַעֲשִׁיר' (מִשְׁלֵי י, כב) – זוֹ הַשַּׁבָּת",
— And this is what they expounded in Bereishit Rabbah (11:1): "'The blessing of Hashem makes rich'—this is the Sabbath",
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שַׁבָּת זוֹכִין לְעֹשֶׁר מִבִּרְכַּת ה', וְזֶהוּ "שָׁלֵם בְּמָמוֹנוֹ":
— whereby through Shabbat one merits holy wealth flowing from Hashem's blessing, which is to be truly whole in one's wealth:

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 86b: “… Just as there, the term ‘this’ is referring to the New Moon, so too, here the term is referring to the New Moon. And similarly, everyone agrees that the Torah was given to the Jewish people on Shabbat, as it is written here in the Ten Commandments: ‘Remember the Shabbat day to keep it holy’ (Exodus 20:8), and it is written there: ‘And Moses said to the people: Remember this day, in which you came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage, for by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from this place; there shall be no leaven eaten’ (Exodus 13:3). Just as there, the mitzva of remembrance was commanded on the very day of the Exodus, so too, here the mitzva of remembrance was commanded on the very day of Shabbat. …”

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 119a: “With regard to the wealthy of other countries, where there are no Sages, by what virtue do they merit their wealth? He said to him: Because they honor Shabbat, as Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said: One time I was hosted at the home of a homeowner in Laodicea and they brought before him a table of gold that was so heavy it required sixteen people to carry it, and there were sixteen chains of silver attached to it, and there were bowls and cups and pitchers and flasks attached to it, and there were all sorts of food, and delicacies, and fragrant spices on it. And when they placed it there they would say: ‘The earth and all that fills it is God’s, the world and all that inhabit it’ (Psalms 24:1). And when they removed it they would say: ‘The heavens are God’s heavens, but the earth He gave to mankind’ (Psalms 115:16). I said to him: My son, what did you do to merit this? He said to me: I was a slaughterer, and when I would come across parts from every animal that I slaughtered that was fine, I would say: This will be for Shabbat. I said to him: Happy are you that you merited this, and blessed is God, Who has afforded you this merit.”

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 11:1: ““God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it.” It is written, “The blessing of Hashem makes rich, and He adds no sorrow with it.” “The blessing of Hashem makes rich”—this is Shabbat, as it is said, “God blessed the seventh day.” “And He adds no sorrow with it”—this is mourning, as it is said, “The king was grieved over his son.””
